land.text: Mauretania Tingitana (capital Tingis) and Mauretania Caesariensis (capital Caesarea), divided along the Mulucha (Moulouya) after Aedemon's revolt

successors.note: Ptolemy was executed in AD 40; the revolt lasted to the surrender of Sabalus in AD 44 (infobox: 'divided into Roman provinces and disestablished in 44 AD'). Cliopatria ends the row in 42.

capitals.name: Volubilis (Walili)
capitals.note: The infobox lists Volubilis first among the capitals; no page opened names a capital before 49 BC (assumption).

capitals.name: Iol (Cherchell)
capitals.note: From 49 BC Bocchus II ruled the east from Iol and Bogud the west from Volubilis; Bocchus II reunited the kingdom in 38 BC. Volubilis stayed a second seat.

capitals.name: Caesarea (Iol, Cherchell)
capitals.note: Juba II and Cleopatra Selene named their new capital Caesaria in honour of Augustus (the Mauretania page: Iol 'was renamed Caesarea'); Volubilis was the secondary capital. Caesarea became the capital of Mauretania Caesariensis.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -225..-213: Cliopatria's first Mauretania shape starts in -212. 'Bagas was the first historically documented king of Mauretania' (the page's table: fl. 225 BC); infobox 'Established: 3rd century BC'. No page gives the extent of Baga's kingdom; the Bocchus I page has the kingdom 'bordered by the Atlantic Ocean and the Moulouya River' (undated), which the -212 shape matches (longitude -8.47 to -2.46).

correction.text: the Moroccan kingdom between the Atlantic and the Moulouya, taken from the -212 shape for Baga's time

keyframe_review.note: 51,321 km2 in Morocco from the Atlantic to the Moulouya (bbox to -2.46): 'bordered by the Atlantic Ocean and the Moulouya River' (page, undated). The Masinissa page: King Bokkar, 'ruler of what is now Morocco', became Masinissa's vassal after Syphax's capture (203), drawn by the ledger. The Mauretania page gives no area, so no infobox check.

69,469 km2: +66 cells on the coast, cell for cell the Moroccan cells that Cliopatria's Carthage shape loses in -197 (ledger gain from carthage, confidence 1). No page opened dates or names the transfer; the Mauretania page gives no area.

Same shape as -197. Bocchus I reigns 'c. 110 - c. 80s BC' but the Numidian share is Jugurtha's price: 'King Bocchus eventually betrayed Jugurtha to the Romans in 105 BCE' and 'By treaty, Bocchus and the Romans divided the kingdom of Numidia between them'. The shape holds -110..-106 only.

New keyframe -105..-92: Cliopatria adds the Numidian west only in -91, fourteen years after the treaty. The Mauretania page: Bocchus lured Jugurtha into a meeting, captured him and handed him to Rome 'in exchange for the western part of Numidian territory'. 561 of the 563 added cells lie inside Cliopatria's Kingdom of Numidia shape of -100.

correction.text: Bocchus I's kingdom with 'the western part of Numidian territory' (to 5.44 E)

keyframe_review.note: 214,867 km2 (Algeria and Morocco, bbox to 5.44 E): 'The kingdom of Mauretania thus extended to Ampsaga' under Bocchus II (the page links the Ampsaga to the Rhummel without describing its course; the shape's eastern edge is 5.44 E). The 49 BC partition between Bocchus II (east, Iol) and Bogud (west, Volubilis) is administrative: Mauretania 'remained a single sovereign kingdom' (Mauretania page).
One year, 214,918 km2: 50 km2 more than the neighbouring shapes, a rounding difference. Bogud's deposition (38 BC) and Bocchus II's death (33) change the king, not the borders.
214,867 km2, the -91 shape again. 'In 38 BC, ... Bocchus II with Octavian's backing, seized control of western Mauretania'; at his death in 33 he 'bequeathed his entire kingdom to Octavian'.

215,292 km2, +0.2 percent. 'In 25 BC Augustus transformed Mauretania into a client kingdom, appointing Juba II'; 'enlarged by territory of Western Numidia' (Juba II page). Cliopatria already holds that land from -91.

Same 215,292 km2. Ptolemy was executed in AD 40 ('Caligula ordered his execution in 40 AD'); Aedemon's revolt followed and Sabalus 'surrendered in 44 AD'; the infobox ends the kingdom in 44. The shape holds 30..44, two years beyond Cliopatria's 42.

ledger.note: 225 BC: Baga, the first documented king of Mauretania. 'Bagas was the first historically documented king of Mauretania' (the page's table: fl. 225 BC); infobox 'Established: 3rd century BC' and 'Mauri kingdoms (3rd century BC - 40 AD)'. The page gives no extent or capital for Baga.

region.text: the Mauri kingdom of Morocco between the Atlantic and the Moulouya

ledger.note: Early 2nd century BC: the Moroccan coast joins Mauretania. Cliopatria's shape grows by 66 cells in -197, exactly the Moroccan cells its Carthage shape loses; no page opened dates or names the transfer.

region.text: the Atlantic and Strait coast of Morocco, held by Carthage

ledger.note: 105 BC: Bocchus I betrays Jugurtha and takes western Numidia. 'King Bocchus eventually betrayed Jugurtha to the Romans in 105 BCE'; 'By treaty, Bocchus and the Romans divided the kingdom of Numidia between them'; the Mauretania page: 'in exchange for the western part of Numidian territory'. The page does not name the land or a river; the region is Cliopatria's -91 addition.

region.text: the western part of Numidian territory

ledger.note: 49 BC: the court divides between two brothers. 'By 49 BC, Mauretania seems to have been partitioned between Bocchus II and Bogud': Bocchus ruled the east from Iol, Bogud the west from Volubilis. The Mauretania page: the kingdom 'remained a single sovereign kingdom, though its administration was divided' after Mastanesosus died in 49.

49-45 BC: Bocchus II takes Cirta with Sittius. 'During the Roman civil war of 49-45 BC, Bocchus and Sittius invaded Numidia'; Cirta was seized 'within a few days', and at the war's end Caesar 'gave Bocchus part of Masinissa II's former territory'. The page gives the span, not the year; -45 is the span's last year. The land lies east of Cliopatria's shape.

region.text: part of Masinissa II's former territory around Cirta

ledger.note: After Caesar's murder (44 BC): Arabio recovers his father's land. 'Arabio, Masinissa's son, recovered it after Caesar's murder.' The page gives no year; 44 is the year of the murder.

region.text: the Numidian land Caesar had given to Bocchus

ledger.note: 38 BC: Bocchus II reunites the kingdom. 'In 38 BC, ... Bocchus II with Octavian's backing, seized control of western Mauretania'; during Bogud's absence in Spain Bocchus 'seized the whole of Mauretania' (Bocchus II page), reconstituting 'a larger Mauretanian kingdom than Bocchus I and Sosus had ever known'. A change of king, not of border.

33 BC: Bocchus II leaves Mauretania to Octavian. 'Upon his own death in 33 BC, Bocchus II bequeathed his entire kingdom to Octavian', who ran it under 'temporary Roman administration for eight years'. Drawn as Roman overlordship, with Cliopatria's shape unchanged.

25 BC: the eight years of Roman administration end. 'In 25 BC Augustus transformed Mauretania into a client kingdom, appointing Juba II' (Mauretania page); the Juba II page: 'then in 25 BC Juba II received it from Augustus'.

25 BC: Juba II rules Mauretania as a client of Rome. Augustus made the final decision between 27 and 25, 'probably for Juba's services in Hispania'; Juba and Cleopatra Selene name the new capital Caesaria (Cherchell). Juba II received Mauretania 'enlarged by territory of Western Numidia' (Juba II page); that land is already this dossier's from the 105 BC gain (ledger -105, the same region), so no separate gain is recorded (reviewer af-02-a removed a -25 gain from roman-empire whose region, the -27 shape minus the -110 shape, repeated the -105 region plus a 0.2 percent redraw).
AD 23: Juba II dies and Ptolemy rules alone. 'Juba II died in AD 23' (the Ptolemy page: 'In AD 23 or 24'), after Ptolemy had been co-ruler from AD 20 or 21. A change of king, not of border.

AD 40: Caligula has Ptolemy executed. Summoned 'sometime in late AD 39' or early 40, he was arrested and executed, 'likely ... sometime after the spring of AD 40'; Caligula 'attempted to annex Mauretania on Ptolemy's death'.

AD 40: Aedemon rebels. After Ptolemy's death his freedman Aedemon 'rallied support and launched a rebellion against Rome'; the page's table dates his rule 40-42, and a second revolt in 42 brought Suetonius Paulinus and Geta (Ptolemy page).
AD 44: the revolt ends. Aedemon's successor Sabalus 'surrendered in 44 AD'.

AD 44: Mauretania becomes two Roman provinces. Mauretania Caesariensis (capital Caesarea) and Mauretania Tingitana (capital Tingis) were created, divided 'along the line of the Mulucha (Muluya) River, about 60 km west of modern Oran'. The Ptolemy page does not date the reorganisation; the Mauretania page has no year for Caesariensis either, and its infobox gives 44. Cliopatria ends the row in 42.

region.text: the whole kingdom, divided into Tingitana and Caesariensis

wars.name: Jugurthine War
wars.outcome: Bocchus I stayed neutral, allied with Jugurtha around 108 (promised a third of his kingdom), lost with him to Marius at the Second Battle of Cirta (106), then betrayed him to Sulla in 105 and took the western part of Numidia by treaty.
wars.note: The page gives 'around 108 BCE' for the alliance and no start year for the war itself, so the span here is Bocchus I's part in it only.

wars.name: Roman civil war in Africa (Bocchus and Sittius in Numidia)

zones.text: Cirta and the Numidian land east of the Ampsaga

wars.outcome: Bocchus and Sittius invaded Numidia on Caesar's side and seized Cirta 'within a few days'; Caesar gave Bocchus part of Masinissa II's land, which Arabio recovered after Caesar's murder.

wars.name: Revolt of Aedemon
wars.outcome: Aedemon, Ptolemy's freedman, rebelled after the execution of AD 40; Sabalus succeeded him and surrendered in 44; Rome made Mauretania Tingitana and Caesariensis.
wars.note: The Ptolemy page has the first revolt suppressed shortly before Claudius's accession in AD 41 and a second revolt in 42 under Suetonius Paulinus and Geta; the Mauretania page ends it in 44.

certainty.note: Frontiers of a nomadic and Mauri kingdom with the Atlantic, the Moulouya and later the Ampsaga as natural limits; none was surveyed. The Mulucha line is the provincial division of AD 44, not a border of the kingdom.

notes:
CLIOPATRIA ROW: one row, -212..42, 8 shapes, no known problem. New keyframes: -225 (Baga, the first documented king) and -105 (the Numidian west, 14 years before Cliopatria draws it); -110 holds only -110..-106 and mauretania_30 holds 30..44; the state ends in AD 44 (infobox), two years after Cliopatria.
ROMAN EMPIRE COUNTERPARTS: the vassal events name roman-empire (a 25 BC gain of Western Numidia from roman-empire was removed in review af-02-a: the land is held from the 105 BC gain), the 33 BC start roman-republic (Octavian's eight years of administration, before the Empire row begins in -31). The Roman Republic dossier (eu-03) records western Numidia going to Bocchus in 46 BC from a page not opened here; this dossier dates the Cirta episode only to 49-45 (confidence 1).
NUMIDIA: the 105 gain and the 46/45 gain name kingdom-of-numidia (Cliopatria -197..-47, af-02); the Numidia dossier should carry the matching losses. The Masinissa page's King Bokkar is the only evidence for the Moroccan kingdom's 203-148 vassalage and is the page's own reading; the end date is a bridge.
CARTHAGE: the 66-cell gain of -197 mirrors the Carthage dossier's loss to mauretania in the same year, both at confidence 1; no page names the land.
WHAT THE PAGES DO NOT GIVE: an area, a capital before 49 BC, the extent of Baga's kingdom, the date of the Jugurthine War, the date of the reorganisation in AD 42 or 44. The Mauretania page names Mastanesosus (80-49 BC) between Bocchus I and the brothers; the Bocchus II page calls Bogud his brother and his cousin.
PAGE BUDGET: five pages for 8 shapes (Mauretania, Bocchus I, Bocchus II, Juba II, Ptolemy of Mauretania) plus the Masinissa page opened for Carthage. No rulers list: the page's table is incomplete.
GAZETTEER: all regions used resolve (Constantine, Mauretania shapes from Cliopatria). Ancient names for the gazetteer agent: Iol/Caesarea (Cherchell), Cirta (Constantine), Volubilis is present, Tingis (Tangier), Lixus.
FIX fx-50 (3 Nov 2026, R008): the two events 'vassal_start -203' and 'vassal_end -148' with counterpart kingdom-of-numidia were removed from this ledger: in a dossier a vassal_start names the vassal as counterpart, so they made Numidia the vassal of Mauretania. The page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masinissa): 'the King Bokkar, ruler of what is now Morocco ... had become a vassal of Masinissa' after the capture of Syphax (the page's French note: 'En 202 avant Jesus-Christ, apres la capture de Syphax, il devint le vassal de Massinissa'); 'he died early in 148 BC without a breach in the alliance'. The relation belongs in kingdom-of-numidia (vassal_start 202 and vassal_end 148, counterpart mauretania; handoff in the fx-50 report; data/patches/m0300-m0201.json events/2, 3, 4 carry it until then).
